title: Eventual descent of finite-presentation flatness
statement: Let I be a directed set and let (S_i)_{i\in I} be an inverse system of quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, where S_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R_i) for Noetherian rings R_i, and let S=\varprojlim_i S_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R). Fix i\in I, let X_i be a finitely presented S_i-scheme [def-pc-scheme], put X=X_i\times_{S_i}S and X_j=X_i\times_{S_i}S_j for j\ge i [def-pc-base-change], and let \mathcal{F}_i be a finitely presented quasi-coherent \mathcal{O}_{X_i}-module. If the pullback of \mathcal{F}_i to X is flat over S [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], then there is j\ge i such that the pullback of \mathcal{F}_i to X_{j'} is flat over S_{j'} for every j'\ge j.

source.place: Lemma 32.10.4, Tag 05LY, with Y_i=S_i (and for later stages since flatness is preserved by base change)

proof.text: Here S_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R_i) is affine; the Noetherian hypothesis on R_i is not used below. Since X_i\to S_i is of finite presentation, hence quasi-compact, and S_i is affine, X_i is quasi-compact, so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover] gives finitely many affine opens U_{1,i},\dots,U_{m,i} covering X_i. Write U_{k,i}=\operatorname{Spec}(B_{k,i}); by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] (with V=S_i) each B_{k,i} is a finitely presented R_i-algebra, and \mathcal{F}_i|_{U_{k,i}}=\widetilde{N_{k,i}} with N_{k,i} a finitely presented B_{k,i}-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] (Stacks Properties, Tag 01PC). The inverse images of U_{k,i} in X_j and X are \operatorname{Spec}(R_j\otimes_{R_i}B_{k,i}) and \operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_{R_i}B_{k,i}) [def-pc-base-change], with pulled-back modules R_j\otimes_{R_i}N_{k,i} and R\otimes_{R_i}N_{k,i}. Since the pullback of \mathcal{F}_i to X is flat over S, the R-module R\otimes_{R_i}N_{k,i} is flat (Stacks Morphisms, Tag 01U4, (1)\Rightarrow(2)).

source.place: Lemma 32.10.4, Tag 05LY, affine-local reduction with Y_i=S_i

proof.text: For each k apply [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-descent] with A_i=R_i (so A_j=R_j and A=R), B_i=B_{k,i} and N_i=N_{k,i}: there is j_k\ge i such that R_j\otimes_{R_i}N_{k,i} is flat over R_j for every j\ge j_k. As I is directed and there are finitely many k, choose j\ge j_1,\dots,j_m.

source.place: Lemma 32.10.4, Tag 05LY, via Algebra Lemma 10.168.1, Tag 02JO (3)

proof.text: Let j'\ge j. The affine opens \operatorname{Spec}(R_{j'}\otimes_{R_i}B_{k,i}), k=1,\dots,m, cover X_{j'}, and on each the pullback of \mathcal{F}_i is flat over the affine S_{j'}=\operatorname{Spec}(R_{j'}) by Step 2. Flatness of a quasi-coherent module over a morphism is local on the source (Stacks Morphisms, Tag 01U4, (3)\Rightarrow(1)), so the pullback of \mathcal{F}_i to X_{j'} is flat over S_{j'}.
